resources.name: Austin Tenants Council – Housing Help for Renters
resources.description: Get help if housing problems started after money harm or family abuse. They help renters with landlord issues, lockouts, and fair housing rights. Staff can explain leases, repairs, and how to stay housed. They can also give classes and one-on-one help. Help is mainly for people in the Austin area. Some help is free for low income renters.

resources.name: Adult Protective Services – Texas Department of Family and Protective Services
resources.description: Get help if someone is hurting, neglecting, or taking money from an older adult. You can report suspected elder abuse, neglect, or financial harm 24 hours a day. Staff can check on safety, help stop the harm, and connect your client to other help. Anyone can call, even if you are not sure what is happening. This help is for people age 65 or older, or adults with disabilities. You do not have to give your name if you are scared.
resources.availability_status: Open 24/7 for reports by phone or online

resources.name: Texas Legal Services Center – Legal Hotline for Texans
resources.description: Get free legal help by phone for people age 60 or older in Texas. They can help with elder abuse, money harm, power of attorney, and other family or money problems. A lawyer or legal helper can explain rights in simple words. They can help plan next steps and may give forms or letters. They cannot go to court in every case, but they can explain choices and safety steps.
resources.address: 1920 E Riverside Dr, Suite A-120, Austin, TX 78741
resources.availability_status: Call for current hours; phone help only for this program

resources.name: AGE of Central Texas – Caregiver and Senior Support
resources.description: Get help for older adults and their helpers, like family or friends. They offer classes, support groups, and one-on-one help to plan care and safety. Staff can talk about money harm, family stress, and safe choices. They can help find adult day care, memory care, and other senior help. Some programs are free or low cost. Your client or a helper can call to talk with staff.
resources.availability_status: Call for current program openings and times

resources.name: Family Eldercare – Financial and Safety Support for Older Adults
resources.description: Get help if an older adult is at risk with money, housing, or safety. They offer money management help, payee help for Social Security checks, and support for people alone. Staff can help protect income and bills if someone has taken money or is at risk. They also help with housing, in-home support, and safety planning. Many programs focus on low income older adults in Central Texas.
resources.availability_status: Some programs may have a waitlist – call to check

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging of the Capital Area (CAPCOG)
resources.description: Get free help for people age 60 or older in Central Texas. They can help with legal aid links, money and benefits questions, and safety for older adults. Staff can explain choices after elder abuse or money harm. They can connect your client to trusted legal help, in-home help, and senior programs. They also have an ombudsman (helper) for people in nursing homes or assisted living.
